title: World Youth Championships day six preview: all-Chinese mixed doubles final as the U19 singles reach the last 16

description: World Youth Championships day six: U19 singles last 16, doubles semi-finals and the all-Chinese mixed doubles final in Istanbul, with every match in UK time.
standfirst: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi meet Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan for the U19 mixed doubles title at about 5pm UK time, after a morning of singles that includes Hana Goda against Heo Yerim.

body: The first under-19 individual title of the World Youth Championships is decided in Istanbul on Thursday, and it will go to China: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi play Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan in the mixed doubles final at about 5pm UK time.

Before that, the boys' and girls' singles reach the last 16, in 16 matches from 9.30am to about 12.30pm UK time, and the four doubles semi-finals follow from 2.30pm. All four Chinese players are on court three times, and all four can still win four gold medals each, having taken both team titles on Monday.
## The big matches
**Wen Ruibo / Jiang Yiyi v Li Hechen / Yao Ruixuan (5pm UK)**

Wen and Jiang were seeded only 16th, but they beat Japan's Kohaku Nakano and Aoba Takahashi 11-9, 11-5, 11-6 in 23 minutes in the semi-finals. The second seeds, Li and Yao, dropped a game against Shunto Iwaida and Mao Takamori before winning in four. Wen, 19, is the world No 14 and the highest-ranked player in Istanbul; Jiang turned 16 last week. Li and Yao are both 17.
**Heo Yerim v Hana Goda (11am UK)**

Egypt's Goda, 18, is the world No 21 and the third seed, and she dropped 21 points in four games against Hong Kong's Mak Ming Shum on Wednesday. Heo, 16, ranked 242nd, came through the day's most up-and-down match, beating Japan's 10th seed Aoba Takahashi 11-6 in the seventh game after losing the fifth 11-2. Heo also has a doubles semi-final at 3pm, with Jeong Yein as the top seeds.
**Wen Ruibo v Steven Moreno (9.30am UK)**

Moreno, 16, of Puerto Rico, is ranked 260th and seeded ninth. He needed seven games to beat Ramon Vila of the Dominican Republic, winning the last 11-1. Wen dropped 18 points in four games against Italy's Danilo Faso. The winner meets Taiwan's Hung Che-Yen or Turkey's Kenan Kahraman in the quarter-finals.
**Priyanuj Bhattacharyya v Emanuel Otalvaro (11.45am UK)**

Otalvaro, the second seed, is 16 and ranked 106th. He won the boys' singles silver at the Youth Olympic Games this month, beating Li Hechen in the quarter-finals in Dakar, [the result that left China without a table tennis medal at the Games](/news/youth-olympic-games-dakar-2026-otalvaro-beats-li-hechen-china-no-medal.html). Bhattacharyya, 18 and ranked 230th, is India's 10th seed. The winner plays Li or Italy's Francesco Trevisan in the quarter-finals, so the Dakar rematch is one round away.
## The home player and the comebacks

Kahraman, 16 and ranked 423rd, beat Iran's fifth seed, Benyamin Faraji, in straight games on Wednesday, with three of the four games going 13-11, 11-9 and 12-10. He now plays Hung, 17, the world No 128, who beat Li Hechen in Monday's boys' team final and took Wen to a deciding game in the match that settled it.

Australia's two comeback winners are both still in. Chulong Nie, 19 and ranked 394th, won the last two games 11-3, 11-3 to beat the third seed, Alan Kurmangaliyev, and meets Tunisia's Wassim Essid, who won the longest match of Wednesday in 63 minutes. Aditya Sareen, 18, came from 3-1 down against Taiwan's seventh seed Lin Chin-Ting and plays Poland's Samuel Michna.
## Jiang, Takamori and the girls' draw

Jiang lost the first game to Lilian Ma of the United States on Wednesday before winning the next four, and she opens the day against France's Alexia Nodin, 16, who beat Turkey's Aybuke Simsek 4-0. Nodin then plays the girls' doubles semi-final with Leana Hochart at 3pm. Takamori, 18, the second seed, meets Australia's Constantina Psihogios, the world No 67, at 10.15am, and Yao plays Russia's Eseniia Shirokova, who beat South Korea's 11th seed Jeong Yein 11-9 in the seventh.

India's Syndrela Das, 17, who beat the seventh seed Sally Moyland, plays Taiwan's Wu Jia-En at 9.30am, and the eighth seed Divyanshi Bhowmick plays Poland's Natalia Bogdanowicz, who came from two games down to beat Germany's Koharu Itagaki. Hong Kong's Su Tsz Tung, the world No 57 and fourth seed, plays Hochart at 11am.
## The doubles semi-finals

Wen and Li, the top seeds in the boys' doubles, play France's Nathan Pilard and Antoine Noirault at 2.30pm, at the same time as Jiang and Yao, the girls' second seeds, play Takamori and Takahashi. At 3pm Kurmangaliyev and Faraji, who both lost their singles on Wednesday, meet South Korea's Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho, and Jeong and Heo play Hochart and Nodin. The doubles finals are on Friday.
## Order of play
Times are approximate and UK time (Istanbul is three hours ahead). Seeds in brackets.

- 9.30am: Wen Ruibo (CHN, 1) v Steven Moreno (PUR, 9); Hung Che-Yen (TPE, 12) v Kenan Kahraman (TUR); Jiang Yiyi (CHN, 1) v Alexia Nodin (FRA, 13); Syndrela Das (IND) v Wu Jia-En (TPE, 9)
- 10.15am: Li Ki Ho (HKG, 4) v Antoine Noirault (FRA); Li Hechen (CHN, 6) v Francesco Trevisan (ITA, 16); Eseniia Shirokova (RUS) v Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 6); Constantina Psihogios (AUS, 12) v Mao Takamori (JPN, 2)
- 11am: Abhinandh Pradhivadhi (IND, 8) v Shunto Iwaida (JPN, 13); Samuel Michna (POL, 15) v Aditya Sareen (AUS); Heo Yerim (KOR) v Hana Goda (EGY, 3); Su Tsz Tung (HKG, 4) v Leana Hochart (FRA, 15)
- 11.45am: Wassim Essid (TUN) v Chulong Nie (AUS); Priyanuj Bhattacharyya (IND, 10) v Emanuel Otalvaro (COL, 2); Bianca Mei-Rosu (ROU, 16) v Wu Ying Syuan (TPE, 5); Divyanshi Bhowmick (IND, 8) v Natalia Bogdanowicz (POL)
- 2.30pm: boys' doubles semi-final, Wen Ruibo / Li Hechen (CHN, 1) v Nathan Pilard / Antoine Noirault (FRA, 4); girls' doubles semi-final, Mao Takamori / Aoba Takahashi (JPN) v Jiang Yiyi / Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 2)
- 3pm: boys' doubles semi-final, Alan Kurmangaliyev / Benyamin Faraji (KAZ/IRI, 3) v Kim Daehwan / Lee Hyeonho (KOR); girls' doubles semi-final, Jeong Yein / Heo Yerim (KOR, 1) v Leana Hochart / Alexia Nodin (FRA, 4)
- 5pm: mixed doubles final, Wen Ruibo / Jiang Yiyi (CHN) v Li Hechen / Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 2)
## How to watch

Eleven's [event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html#matches) has live scores, the full draws and the order of play, and shows the stream whenever one is live. All the singles are best of seven games and the doubles best of five. The singles quarter-finals and the boys' and girls' doubles finals are on Friday; their times had not been published early on Thursday.
## Wednesday in brief

Three of the top seven boys' seeds went out in the last 32: Kurmangaliyev to Nie, Faraji to Kahraman and Lin to Sareen. In the girls' draw Das beat Moyland, Heo beat Takahashi and Bogdanowicz beat Itagaki, while Wen, Jiang, Goda and Otalvaro all won in straight games or close to it. The details are in Eleven's [day five review](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-day-five-review-results-highlights.html).
